title: Order Flow Imbalance and Short-Horizon BTC/USDT Returns: A Signal That Kept Needing More Scrutiny
abstract: <div> We test whether order-flow imbalance (OFI), defined per Cont, Kukanov &amp; Stoikov (2014), </div> <div> predicts short-horizon (1–10 second) mid-price returns in BTC/USDT, using L2 order-book </div> <div> data reconstructed from Binance.US’s diff-depth stream. </div> <div> <br> </div> <div> We evaluate this across three successive extensions of the same capture (∼7, ∼9, and ∼17 </div> <div> days), using an identical walk-forward pipeline: purge/embargo at fold boundaries, Newey- </div> <div> West HAC inference, and moving-block bootstrap confidence intervals, benchmarked against </div> <div> a training-mean forecast and two naive alternatives: signed trade-flow imbalance and a same- </div> <div> horizon AR(1) trailing return. </div> <div> <br> </div> <div> The out-of-sample result reversed twice as the sample grew. On ∼7 days, OFI showed </div> <div> significant positive R2 (0.17%–1.00%), decaying monotonically with horizon and surviving a </div> <div> permutation placebo test. On ∼9 days, the pooled result turned null or negative at every horizon. </div> <div> On ∼17 days, after fixing two data-pipeline issues identified through fold-level diagnostics and </div> <div> adding purge/embargo, it turned positive again (R2 0.13%–1.06%), again surviving a placebo </div> <div> test. Fold-level decomposition throughout shows a coefficient that never changes sign, with </div> <div> noisy but eventually net-favorable out-of-sample fit. Univariately, AR(1) matches or beats </div> <div> OFI at every horizon except 10s and trade-flow imbalance is never significant; a combined </div> <div> OFI-plus-AR(1) specification shows both predictors survive together, with the combined model </div> <div> outperforming either alone at every horizon. </div> <div> <br> </div> <div> We interpret this as a small, real, direction-consistent effect that carries information beyond </div> <div> simple price momentum but is difficult to detect reliably below roughly two weeks of single- </div> <div> symbol, single-venue data. The repeated reversals are also the paper’s central methodological </div> <div> point: a single walk-forward result, however clean, should be treated as provisional until it </div> <div> survives a deliberate attempt to break it. </div>
